newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate up 20 bps to 11.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate up 20 bps to 11.3 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate inched up 20 basis points to 11.3 percent on Wednesday, pushed up by higher term rates in brisk trade.
Daily settlements reached 40.6 million kuna, leaving a surplus of 20 million on the supply side.
All but 10.9 million was accounted for by fresh loans, mostly call money granted at a steady weighted rate of 10.5 percent.
Insurers extended a total of 8.4 million kuna, at 9-14 percent for one-week borrowings and 17-19 percent for one one-month money.
Banks rolled over one- and two-week loans at 14 percent.
The central bank calculated its kuna midrates for Thursday weaker at 6.1346 against the dollar and firmer at 3.5758 against German mark. -- Metka Jelenc, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
